$comment: The single registry of tells. min: occurrences needed before a tell counts toward the score (a finding marked strong counts alone; W1/W2 count only when the checker marks them strong, i.e. dense). The checker, the static scanner, the report and references/tells.md all key on `id`. weight: 3 = strong tell on its own, 2 = clear tell, 1 = weak alone, counts in combination. scope: app (product/admin/dashboard), landing (marketing), both. detect: dom (rendered-page checker), static (source scanner), manual (read the code/screen).

tells.title: Decorative gradient
tells.short: Gradient washes on surfaces, sidebars, headers, buttons or badges that carry no information.
tells.fix: Flat token colour. Keep a gradient only where it encodes data (a heat scale, a progress fill).

tells.title: Gradient text
tells.short: Headline text filled with a gradient (background-clip: text).
tells.fix: Solid ink. Emphasis comes from size, weight and position, not a fill.

tells.title: Default indigo/violet primary
tells.short: Primary buttons and accents in the framework-default indigo/violet (hue 240-290, e.g. #6366F1, #8B5CF6).
tells.fix: Derive the primary from the brand. If the brand truly is violet, declare it in .slop.json.

tells.title: Accent sprawl
tells.short: Many saturated hues used as solid fills; colour on chrome rather than on data; each card its own colour.
tells.fix: Neutral UI, one brand colour for action and selection, semantic colours only for state.

tells.title: Neon on near-black
tells.short: A near-black page with one acid accent and glowing elements, with no light theme.
tells.fix: Pick the theme for the audience. Drop the glow; contrast does the work.

tells.title: Untouched framework palette
tells.short: Tailwind/shadcn stock swatches used as the brand (indigo-500, violet-600, slate-900, shadcn default HSL vars).
tells.fix: Define project tokens on :root and use them everywhere.

tells.title: Cream + serif + terracotta
tells.short: The 2026 'tasteful default': warm cream ground (#F4F1EA-ish), serif display face, terracotta/clay or sage accent.
tells.fix: Do not swap one default for another. Choose palette and type from the brand and audience.

tells.title: Default face as the whole identity
tells.short: Inter, Roboto, Arial, Open Sans or the system stack as the only family, for display and body alike.
tells.fix: Keep a neutral body face if you like; give headings a deliberate choice. Declare an intended default in .slop.json.

tells.title: Trend display face
tells.short: The second-wave defaults: Space Grotesk, Instrument Serif, Fraunces, Syne, Geist, Playfair as display.
tells.fix: Choose for the brand, not because it is the current safe pick.

tells.title: Eyebrows and tracked caps
tells.short: Tiny uppercase, letter-spaced labels above headings, on section titles, nav, table heads.
tells.fix: Sentence case, untracked, the body face. The heading already names the section.

tells.title: One accented word in a headline
tells.short: A single word in a heading set in italic serif or a different colour.
tells.fix: One style per heading. Let the sentence carry the emphasis.

tells.title: Monospace as costume
tells.short: Monospace used for labels, captions or meta that are not code, IDs or aligned figures.
tells.fix: Body face with tabular-nums for numbers; mono only for code and identifiers.

tells.title: Many near-equal sizes
tells.short: Lots of font sizes a pixel or two apart instead of a few clearly separated steps.
tells.fix: A scale of about five sizes, far apart (e.g. 12/14/16/20/28).

tells.title: Text under 12px
tells.short: Visible text set below 12px.
tells.fix: 12px floor (Cloudscape, Carbon); shorten the text instead of shrinking it.

tells.title: Stranded last word
tells.short: A multi-line heading whose last line holds a single word.
tells.fix: text-wrap: balance on headings; rewrite if it still strands.

tells.title: One big radius on everything
tells.short: A single radius of 12px or more on most boxes, regardless of hierarchy.
tells.fix: Radius per nesting level: smaller inside, larger outside; controls and chips share one small radius.

tells.title: Mixed chip shapes and heights
tells.short: Pills next to square chips, or several chip heights, for the same kind of label; pill buttons in a dense app.
tells.fix: One shape and one height per kind of label. Pills are fine when consistent (Carbon, Primer).

tells.title: Coloured side stripe
tells.short: A 3-4px coloured border on one edge of a card, alert, banner or list item, used as decoration.
tells.fix: Put the colour on the element that means it (an icon, a status label); keep the card border uniform. An edge that marks current position (active nav item, selected row, diff gutter, blockquote) is fine.

tells.title: Soft shadow under every card
tells.short: Resting cards and panels lifted by the same soft grey drop shadow.
tells.fix: Group with a border or whitespace. Shadows belong to overlays (menus, dialogs, popovers) and draggable items.

tells.title: Border + shadow on one resting box
tells.short: A resting box with a border and a drop shadow (and sometimes a ring) at once.
tells.fix: Pick one: border or elevation.

tells.title: Glow and dramatic shadow
tells.short: Coloured blurred halos, glowing buttons, text-shadow, very large drop shadows.
tells.fix: No coloured shadows. Buttons rest flat (M3 level 0); overlays use the system's shadow step.

tells.title: Glassmorphism
tells.short: backdrop-filter blur on translucent panels, navs and cards as decoration.
tells.fix: Opaque surfaces. Blur only for controls floating over moving content (Apple HIG).

tells.title: Cards inside cards
tells.short: A bordered or shadowed box inside another, inside another.
tells.fix: One container level; inside it use spacing, dividers and headings.

tells.title: Aurora/blob background
tells.short: Blurred colour blobs, mesh or aurora gradients, grid-and-glow backdrops behind the hero.
tells.fix: A plain ground, or real imagery of the product.

tells.title: KPI tile row
tells.short: 3-6 identical cards, each with an icon tile, a big (often coloured) number, a caption or a +12% chip.
tells.fix: Numbers as type in a compact row or inside the table header; no icon tiles, no captions repeating the label.

tells.title: Icon in a tinted tile
tells.short: A glyph inside a coloured square or circle beside a heading, card, row or feature.
tells.fix: The glyph alone, coloured like its text, or no icon. No icons on section headings (Cloudscape).

tells.title: Icon soup chip
tells.short: One small label carrying an icon, words, a tint and a border.
tells.fix: Words alone, or an icon-only control with a tooltip. 'Don't include icons on badges' (Cloudscape).

tells.title: Centred hero, then three icon cards
tells.short: Centred headline with two CTAs, followed by a grid of 3 or 6 same-shaped feature cards with icons.
tells.fix: Lead with the product itself (a real screenshot, a demo, the main job); vary the rhythm of sections.

tells.title: Pill badge above the hero
tells.short: A rounded 'New: ...' or sparkle chip sitting above the H1.
tells.fix: Delete it; put real news in the headline or a changelog link.

tells.title: 01 / 02 / 03 markers
tells.short: Zero-padded numbers on sections or cards that are not a sequence.
tells.fix: Number only real steps; otherwise drop the markers.

tells.title: Fake window chrome
tells.short: Three traffic-light dots drawn around a screenshot or code block.
tells.fix: Show the screenshot as it is, or a real device frame if context matters.

tells.title: Emoji and sparkles as icons
tells.short: Emoji in headings, nav, bullets or buttons; the four-point sparkle on anything 'AI'.
tells.fix: One icon set, used to supplement text; name AI features by what they do.

tells.title: Decorative status dots
tells.short: A coloured dot on every chip or row, often pulsing, repeating what the label already says.
tells.fix: Status as icon/shape + text (Carbon, Cloudscape); show a marker only where it changes a decision.

tells.title: Same badge on every row
tells.short: A table column where every row carries the same coloured badge.
tells.fix: Plain text for the normal case; highlight only the exception.

tells.title: Middle-dot meta strings and glued arrows
tells.short: 'A · B · C' joins, 'WORD — fragment' labels, '→' appended to links and buttons.
tells.fix: Separate cells, a second line, or a comma. A button says what it does without an arrow.

tells.title: Dash for an empty value
tells.short: "N/A", "null", "none", or a dash standing for a missing value outside a dense table.
tells.fix: One empty-value convention: a muted dash only in dense tables (Cloudscape), words such as "Not set" in detail views and forms; never "N/A".

tells.title: Competing primary buttons
tells.short: Several solid filled buttons visible at once.
tells.fix: One primary per page or area (Cloudscape, Carbon, Atlassian, Fluent, Primer); others outline, subtle or link.

tells.title: Hero or welcome banner inside the app
tells.short: A marketing-style hero, greeting banner or illustration at the top of a working screen.
tells.fix: Start with the user's work: the list, the queue, the next action.

tells.title: Charts standing in for content
tells.short: Sparklines, donuts or progress rings that fill space without supporting a decision.
tells.fix: A chart only when the shape of the data answers a question; otherwise a number or a table.

tells.title: Endless motion
tells.short: Infinite animations that signal nothing: pulsing dots, rippling CTAs, nudging arrows, shimmer outside loading.
tells.fix: Nothing loops unless it marks a real ongoing state (loading, recording, a live call) and stops when the state ends; mark those role="status".

tells.title: Hover lift and scale
tells.short: Cards and buttons that translate up or scale on hover.
tells.fix: Change colour or border on hover; keep layout still (Uncodixfy, no-slop-ui).

tells.title: transition: all
tells.short: Transitions on every property, usually with one shared duration.
tells.fix: Transition only the properties that change, 50-150ms for hover/press (Atlassian, Carbon).

tells.title: Fade-up on every section
tells.short: Every section fades and rises into view with the same timing.
tells.fix: At most one deliberate entrance; content is simply there.

tells.title: Motion without a reduced-motion path
tells.short: Animations with no prefers-reduced-motion rule.
tells.fix: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) removes non-essential motion.

tells.title: Buzzword copy
tells.short: Unlock, supercharge, seamless, elevate, unleash, revolutionise; 'not just X, it's Y'; 'all-in-one platform'.
tells.fix: Say what the product does, with a concrete noun and verb.

tells.title: Generic call to action
tells.short: 'Get started', 'Learn more', 'Submit', 'Click here' as button labels.
tells.fix: Verb + object: 'Create meeting', 'Save changes' (Anthropic, Cloudscape).

tells.title: Copy that explains the screen
tells.short: Subtitles restating the title, section notes describing the UI, developer text leaking into the page.
tells.fix: Delete it. A header line may carry data (a count), not an explanation.

tells.title: Exclamation marks and cheer
tells.short: Exclamation marks, 'Oops!', 'Awesome!' in UI copy.
tells.fix: Calm statements; errors name the problem and the recovery (Atlassian, Fluent).

tells.title: Template leakage
tells.short: Lorem ipsum, [Name], {{placeholders}}, John Doe, Acme Inc, example.com in the shipped UI.
tells.fix: Real data, or an honest empty state.

tells.title: Invented social proof
tells.short: Round stat banners (10k+ users, 99.9% uptime, 4.9 stars), 'Trusted by' logo walls, testimonials without sources.
tells.fix: Only claims you can source; otherwise leave them out.

tells.title: Low-contrast text
tells.short: Body text under 4.5:1 against its background, often grey-on-grey or grey on colour.
tells.fix: 4.5:1 for body, 3:1 for large text and UI marks (WCAG 2.2).

tells.title: Focus ring removed
tells.short: outline: none / outline-none without a visible :focus-visible replacement.
tells.fix: A visible :focus-visible ring in the brand colour.

tells.title: Only the happy path
tells.short: No designed empty, filtered-empty, loading, error or long-content states.
tells.fix: Design each state with real, hostile data: long names, zero items, failures.

tells.title: A toast for every action
tells.short: Success toasts for actions whose result is already visible on screen.
tells.fix: Toast only when the result is off-screen, delayed or failed.
